correctness.rationale: Each nonempty antichain of nonempty coalitions gives exactly one monotone truth table with losing empty and winning grand coalition. The branch-on-pivot recursion generates each once by including or excluding the pivot, deleting only comparable sets when including it. Properness is then exactly the exclusion of two complementary wins. The independent replay evaluates every eligible substitution for each ordered pair and compares the raw minimum-winner counts, which have a common positive normalization. Canonical representatives are minima over all player permutations. The replay found proper-game counts 1,3,11,80,2645 and isomorphism counts 1,2,5,14,86; no violations through four, 460 at five in the nine given orbits, and histogram 300/120/40. It checked each displayed quota-weight representation against all 32 coalitions, as well as the normalized vectors and strict weight and index directions. The reported fraction 92/529 is correct and simplifies further to 4/23. Greater or equal weight implies Isbell dominance, so the lower boundary also holds for local monotonicity in proper weighted games.
residual_risks: No exhaustiveness at n≥6 or minimality of the displayed weights is asserted.

evidence: For i dominating j, let I,J be the stripped minimal winning families containing only i or only j of the pair. They live on at most three other players. Every Y in J contains an X in I by substitution and minimality. If both families are nonempty, properness gives X∩Y nonempty for every cross pair. A strict Public Good loss for i is |J|>|I|.

If |I|=1, at least two incomparable Y must contain its sole nonempty X; on at most three ground elements this forces a singleton X and exactly two size-two supersets in J. Thus DP_j exceeds DP_i by 2/3−1/2 before normalization, with common minimal winners canceling.

If |I|≥2, the only possible case is |I|=2, |J|=3, using the maximum antichain size on three elements. The size-three antichain must consist of all singletons or all pairs. For singletons, covering by nonempty X requires three distinct X. For pairs, every X must meet all pairs and therefore have size at least two, so covering the pairs again requires three X. Both are impossible.

The dominance is strict: mutual dominance gives a swap automorphism and equal Public Good counts. Strict Isbell dominance entails strictly greater Shapley–Shubik score for i, by the positively weighted sum of differences between the two players' substitution values. Thus every Public Good failure forces a strict DP/SS reversal. Conversely, all nine earlier tabulated families exhibit a Public Good failure by exact direct checks.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The earlier complete theorem restricts every possible Public Good failure to its already-tabulated layer, and row evaluation gives equality of the two sets through five players. The new 300/120/40 counts are the orbit-size sums for one, two, or three loss directions read from those same graphs; they are not an independently new census. The frozen finding asserts the marginal classification, not a novel structural theorem explaining the cross-index coincidence.

value.rationale: Dominance is a motivated axiom and a genuinely new first failing layer would be worthwhile. Here the combinatorial classification, weighted witnesses, and counts of games are recovered from an existing exact nine-row table by a short reduction. The remaining normalized index columns, loss-direction labels and their histogram are routine row evaluations and orbit-size sums, not an independently motivated exact invariant that survives removal of the covered census. A structural study of why the first layers coincide would be a different contribution; it is not the frozen finding and no repaired claim is submitted.
residual_risks: The judgement concerns the stated marginal census, not the broader scientific interest of comparing coalition-based indices.
